channel.title: GOLFRAW
channel.description: Golf news without the press-release language. Evidence first, opinion labeled.

item.title: A Home Solheim Cup, and the Dutch Star Can't Play
item.description: Dewi Weber is ranked ahead of three of Europe's captain's picks. She can't be selected for the Solheim Cup in her own country because of an LET rule.

item.title: He Won at 25 Under. This Week Is the Opposite.
item.description: Koivun won the 3M Open at 25 under. TPC Southwind has seven par 4s over 450 yards and water on 11 holes. The first real test of a 21-year-old's season.

item.title: He Shot 59 and It Only Got Him Into a Playoff
item.description: Frankie Harris shot a 12-under 59 to win the Pinnacle Bank Championship — but Alistair Docherty birdied his last three to force extra holes.

item.title: Montgomerie Has Been Right About This Since 2020
item.description: Cameron Young averages 312 yards this year using a ball that meets the 2030 rules — one further than last season. Why golf's rollback just got paused again.

item.title: Playing With a Pro Costs $10,000. Or $200.
item.description: PGA Tour pro-ams run $2,500–$10,000 a head. Your local PGA section runs them for $200–$400, at private clubs. How pro-ams work and what pros expect of you.

item.title: The Three Feet That Decide Whether You Three-Putt
item.description: Tour players hole 99.42% from three feet and 70.98% from six. Everything about three-putting is which one you leave yourself.

item.title: The Tournament the Tour Demoted Is the Hardest One
item.description: Detroit gave up three 61s. Sedgefield gave up 36 rounds under 66. TPC Southwind is the same par and the hardest of the three — and it's being relegated.

item.title: The Winning Team Finished Six Over Par
item.description: Crushers GC won LIV New York at six over — the highest winning team score in league history. Niemann took the individual title wire to wire at 16 under.

item.title: One Player In, One Out. The Rest Ran Out of Season.
item.description: Michael Brennan won and jumped to 47th. Steven Fisk missed the cut and fell to 71st. Koepka, Day, Bradley and Finau are all out. The final FedExCup 70.

item.title: Playing Golf in Your Fifties: What Distance Loss Actually Costs You
item.description: Playing golf in your 50s changes carry, approach clubs and suitable course length. Learn when to move up a tee and protect your score.

item.title: Scheffler Isn't at a Disadvantage at the Tour Championship. He Just Has No Advantage.
item.description: The FedExCup leader no longer starts 10 under at the Tour Championship. That isn't a disadvantage — it's no advantage. Why the difference matters in 2026.

item.title: Lowest Round in LET History Friday. Four-Putt Sunday.
item.description: Charley Hull shot 62 to equal the lowest round in Ladies European Tour history, then four-putted the 17th while leading. Anna Huang, 17, eagled the last to win.

item.title: Michigan Pro Golf Faces an Uncertain Future in 2027
item.description: Michigan could lose three men's pro golf events before 2027. See the latest on the Rocket Classic, LIV Golf, Ally Challenge and LPGA stops.

item.title: Lee Westwood Is 53, Four Back, and Done With Expectations
item.description: Everyone ran the 'brain-dead' quote. The one after it is better: Westwood on why he stopped setting expectations — and he's four off the lead at 53.

item.title: Eighth in Iron Play, 116th in Putting: The Brutal Math Behind Brooks Koepka's Wyndham Stand
item.description: Koepka is 8th on Tour in approach play and 116th in putting. He withdrew from Detroit with a hand injury. Now he needs a massive week at Sedgefield.

item.title: DeChambeau Says He'd Play "Wherever They'll Let Me." The Man Who Decides Says No.
item.description: DeChambeau says he'd love to play PGA Tour events again. The Tour's CEO said "no merger, no conversations" the same week. And he turned down the way back.

item.title: She Won by Six and Five on Thursday. On Friday She Lost on the 19th.
item.description: Rianne Malixi beat the world No. 14 amateur by six and five, then lost on the 19th hole the next day. What match play does that stroke play never does.

item.title: You Can Play With a Professional Golfer. It Doesn't Have to Cost $10,000.
item.description: PGA Tour pro-ams run $2,500–$10,000 a head. Your local PGA section runs them for $200–$400, at private clubs. How pro-ams work and how to actually get in.

item.title: 5 of America's Best Golf Courses Are in Washington — Here's Where to Play Them (2026)
item.description: Five Washington golf courses made Golfweek's 2026 list of America's 200 best modern courses — not four. See the rankings, locations, and which ones you can play.

item.title: Jason Day's Streak Ended on a Friday in Greensboro
item.description: Jason Day missed the cut at Sedgefield and ended a run of 19 consecutive FedExCup Playoff seasons. Bradley and Finau survived on the number.

item.title: The Mystery Investor Has a Name. It Lends Money to Bryson DeChambeau's Agency.
item.description: Bloomberg and the FT name BC Partners as LIV's investor — a lender to Bryson DeChambeau's agency. And LIV quietly lost its feeder tour to the PGA Tour.

item.title: A 61 Led in Greensboro. A 64 Led in New Jersey.
item.description: Two tournaments, one Thursday. Sedgefield gave up 36 rounds under 66. Bedminster's leader shot 64 and won by two. What 520 yards actually does.

item.title: He Needed to Win. One Round Later, He's Projected 52nd.
item.description: Hossler went from 122nd to a projected 52nd in a single round. Koepka needs a top four for a spot that pays him nothing. Inside the Wyndham bubble.

item.title: He Threw a Bottle at a Bin From Four Feet. He Missed.
item.description: DeChambeau shot 76 at Bedminster — his worst LIV round of the year — and lost it with a bin on the fifth tee. Why the clip is the least of his problems.

item.title: The Last Signature Event Ended on a Missed 4-Footer
item.description: Hovland beat Scheffler in a Monday playoff at the Travelers after storms, a 61 from nine back, and a missed four-footer. What the Tour's restructure can't buy.

item.title: LIV Bedminster Purse: $20M, $4M to Win
item.description: LIV Golf New York at Bedminster carried a $20 million individual purse, with Joaquín Niemann earning $4 million for the victory.

item.title: LIV Says It's Saved. It Won't Say By Whom.
item.description: LIV Golf says it has a signed lead investor and players will be majority owners. It won't name the investor or the amount. What was actually announced.

item.title: America's Biggest "Golf Deal" Search Is a Resort
item.description: Destination searches beat equipment 3.5 to 1 in US "golf deals" data, and advertisers pay double for them. What the category is really selling you.

item.title: Smith Turned Down the Exit in February
item.description: Cam Smith says he'd "100%" return to the PGA Tour if LIV folded. But he turned down the exit route in February — and PIF pulled its funding in April.

item.title: 7-Wood vs 3-Iron: What Aussie Golfers Actually Search
item.description: Australians search for a 7-wood three times more than a 3-iron. The loft numbers, the one downside nobody mentions, and why the club has three names.

item.title: Wyndham Championship Bubble: Koivun Leads by 12 Points
item.description: Jackson Koivun enters the 2026 Wyndham Championship holding the 70th FedExCup spot by just 12 points. What Sedgefield's positional layout means for the playoff bubble.

item.title: The Tour's Answer to Detroit? A Quarter-Inch of Grass
item.description: Detroit spent $16.1m to get harder and gave up three 61s. Sedgefield defends itself with a quarter-inch of rough and 12½-foot greens.

item.title: Wyndham Championship 2026 Preview: Odds, Picks & Bubble Stakes
item.description: 2026 Wyndham Championship preview: Cameron Young defends at Sedgefield as FedExCup playoff race hits fever pitch. Betting tips, fantasy picks, course guide and key stats.

item.title: Wyndham Odds & FedExCup Bubble: Day & Bradley Scenarios
item.description: Jason Day and Keegan Bradley arrive at the 2026 Wyndham Championship on the FedExCup bubble. Explore odds, playoff scenarios and Sedgefield course trends before you bet.

item.title: Why Golfers Are Abandoning Texas Scrambles
item.description: Why are golfers turning their backs on Texas Scrambles? New survey data exposes handicap manipulation, unfair scoring, and the real reasons players are losing interest.

item.title: 8 Big Names Missing the 2026 Solheim Cup (And Why They're Out)
item.description: From 0.9-point Heartbreaks to pregnancy and broken wrists, here are 8 major stars missing the 2026 Solheim Cup at Bernardus Golf and why.

item.title: 2027 Ryder Cup Europe Qualifying Schedule Confirmed
item.description: Team Europe's 2027 Ryder Cup qualifying schedule is confirmed, starting at the British Masters. Key dates, points structure, eligibility rules and what it means for Adare Manor.

item.title: Players Get Equity "Instead of Cash," Says LIV CEO
item.description: LIV Golf says players will become majority owners. Its CEO then said the equity comes "instead of cash." What that actually means for the league.

item.title: LIV Golf Terminates Staff Contracts Amid Bankruptcy Speculation
item.description: LIV Golf has reportedly terminated staff contracts with 30 days' notice as the Saudi-backed league faces bankruptcy speculation and fights for survival beyond 2026.

item.title: The 4 Golf Majors Explained: Winners, Venues & Prestige
item.description: A comprehensive guide to golf's four majors: The Masters, PGA Championship, U.S. Open, and The Open Championship. Includes 20-year winner tables and history.
